mathgap.title: Signed 'has N more than'
mathgap.principle: When a statement says 'X has N more than Y', translate it to X = Y + N (adding N to Y).
mathgap.when_to_apply: Whenever the phrasing explicitly uses 'has N more than' without mentioning a combined total.
mathgap.example: Interpreting 'X has 3 more than Y' as X = Y - 3.

mathgap.title: Allow negative differences
mathgap.principle: For equations that explicitly refer to a signed difference (e.g., 'the difference between A and B is ...'), keep the sign; allow the result to be negative if the order of the names implies it.
mathgap.when_to_apply: When a statement uses the phrase 'difference between A and B' without 'has more than'.
mathgap.example: Forcing the equation A - B = 5 to be non‑negative even when B > A.

mathgap.title: Model transfers as net changes
mathgap.principle: For a transfer 'X gives N to Y', subtract N from X and add N to Y; apply both changes to the current counts.
mathgap.when_to_apply: Whenever a statement describes a person giving a fixed number of items to another.
mathgap.example: Updating only the giver's count and forgetting to increase the receiver's count.

mathgap.title: Systematic equation solving
mathgap.principle: Introduce a variable for each person, translate every statement into a linear equation, then solve the resulting system (using substitution, elimination, or matrix methods).
mathgap.when_to_apply: For any puzzle with multiple relational statements.
mathgap.example: Attempting to guess numbers without forming equations.

mathgap.title: Combined sum interpretation
mathgap.principle: For statements like 'X has N more than Y and Z combined', first sum Y and Z, then add N: X = (Y + Z) + N.
mathgap.when_to_apply: When the phrasing mentions a combined total of two or more people.
mathgap.example: Interpreting 'X has 5 more than Y and Z combined' as X = Y + 5, ignoring Z.

mathgap.title: Increase by factor interpretation
mathgap.principle: When a statement says 'the number of X increases by k times', multiply the original amount by k: new = old × k.
mathgap.when_to_apply: When the wording uses 'times' or 'multiplied by'.
mathgap.example: Treating 'doubles' as adding the original amount instead of multiplying.

mathgap.title: Equal split and redistribution handling
mathgap.principle: If a person splits all their items equally among a set of recipients, set the splitter's count to zero and give each recipient an equal share of the total.
mathgap.when_to_apply: When a statement describes splitting all items equally among others.
mathgap.example: Leaving the splitter's count unchanged after a split.

mathgap.title: Sequential direct assignments
mathgap.principle: When multiple statements assign a direct count to the same person, treat them as occurring in order; later statements overwrite earlier ones.
mathgap.when_to_apply: When a person receives more than one explicit count.
mathgap.example: Assuming both 'A has 5' and later 'A has 7' hold simultaneously.

mathgap.title: Absolute difference for 'has more than' in relational equations
mathgap.principle: In equations of the form 'the number of X that Y has more than Z equals …', interpret the left side as a non‑negative absolute difference |Y − Z|.
mathgap.when_to_apply: When a relational equation uses the phrase 'has more than' on the left side.
mathgap.example: Treating 'the number of apples X has more than Y equals 3' as X − Y = 3, allowing a negative result.

mathgap.title: Mixed absolute‑signed difference equation
mathgap.principle: When a statement equates an absolute difference (e.g., 'X has more than Y') to a signed difference (e.g., 'difference between A and B'), translate to |X − Y| = (A − B). Ensure the right‑hand side is non‑negative; if it is negative, swap A and B or re‑examine the wording.
mathgap.when_to_apply: For relational equations that mix 'has more than' with 'difference between …'.
mathgap.example: Interpreting 'the number of carrots X has more than Y equals the difference between A and B' as X − Y = A − B (ignoring the absolute nature of the left side).

mathgap.description: Treating 'X has N' as an initial count before transfers
mathgap.why_it_happens: The model assumes that a statement giving a concrete count sets a fixed baseline, then applies later transfer statements on top of it, ignoring that the count may already reflect transfers.
mathgap.how_to_avoid: Treat 'X has N' as the current count after all prior actions; when a transfer occurs, update both giver and receiver accordingly without assuming the initial count is pre‑transfer.

mathgap.why_it_happens: The model often forgets to zero out the splitter or to divide equally among recipients.
mathgap.how_to_avoid: When a person splits all items equally, set their count to zero and distribute the total equally among the recipients.

mathgap.description: Applying transfers in the wrong direction
mathgap.why_it_happens: The model may reverse the giver and receiver when updating counts.
mathgap.how_to_avoid: For 'X gives N to Y', subtract N from X and add N to Y.

mathgap.description: Misinterpreting 'increase by N times' as addition rather than multiplication
mathgap.why_it_happens: The phrasing 'times' is taken as an additive increment.
mathgap.how_to_avoid: Treat 'increases by k times' as multiplication: new = old × k.

mathgap.description: Treating 'has more than' in relational equations as signed difference, leading to negative values
mathgap.why_it_happens: The model applies X − Y = N directly, ignoring that the phrase implies a non‑negative absolute gap.
mathgap.how_to_avoid: Interpret the left side as |X − Y|, a non‑negative value.
